title: Remediation & Data Exit — negotiation scratchpad
content:
Notes to self — high level objective:
- Make sure vendor obligations enable clean, auditable data export and complete removal of customer data from multi-tenant caches/KV layers within a bounded timeline.
- Preserve Redwood’s IP posture: we cannot concede rights to model weights or the right to re-use customer prompts to retrain without explicit consent.

Key clauses to watch (priority order):
1) Breach remediation / incident response (high priority)
   - Vendor: immediate notification + 72-hour initial report + 30-day remediation plan?
   - Our ask: 24-hour initial notification for incidents involving customer data or model-exfiltration; 7-day detailed remediation plan; weekly status calls until closed.
   - Script: "We treat model- or data-exfiltration as a critical incident. 24-hour notice is non-negotiable — anything slower undermines customer trust and our compliance obligations."
   - Escalation: include SLAs for response time and named contacts; require runbook access for incident validation.

2) Data export / exit assistance (very high)
   - Must define format(s): JSONL (raw tokens + metadata), Parquet for large exports, and an option for SQL dump for structured metadata.
   - Timeline: final export availability within 14 days of termination (prefer 7 days for enterprise).
   - Walk-back assistance: 30 days of transition support post-termination with N hours of engineer support included (ask: 40 hours).
   - Guarantees: vendor must certify deletion across caches, backups, logs, and third-party subprocessors within 60 days (or earlier on a staging-by-staging basis).
   - Proof: require attestation + hash manifests and optional on-site/auditor access for critical customers.
   - Script: "We need export in a vendor-neutral format and a certified deletion attestation. We cannot accept ambiguous ‘reasonable efforts’."

3) KMS / key rotation / crypto custody
   - If they hold keys, require customer-controlled KMS or a BYOK option.
   - Key rotation events must not break ability to decrypt archives for export.
   - Ask for a key-escrow/rotation playbook and confirmation that exports are decryptable by customer with existing keys.

4) Subprocessors & downstream sharing
   - List all subprocessors liveness + change-notice window (30 days).
   - Right to object to new subprocessors for security/compliance reasons; if objected, vendor must propose remediation/alternative.
   - Require contractual flow-down for deletion obligations and incident notification.

5) Liability cap carveouts and indemnity (sensitive)
   - Standard cap is fine but carve out for intentional IP theft, data exfiltration, breach of confidentiality, and gross negligence.
   - Indemnity: push to limit to third-party IP claims and data breach costs — avoid broad indemnities for model outputs that reflect ambiguous ownership.
   - Script: "We're comfortable with a commercial cap, but not for willful misappropriation or intentional exfiltration — those are uncapped."

6) Model output IP / ownership of outputs
   - We must keep customer rights to use outputs for their business (as-is).
   - Vendor may not claim ownership of customer-provided prompts, labeled data, or derivative outputs used to train models unless explicit, compensated license.
   - If vendor requests usage rights for model improvement, require opt-in checkbox per-customer (no surprise training).

7) Retention & backups
   - Define maximum retention windows for PII and for non-PII telemetry used for model improvement; default: 30 days for raw logs unless customer consents longer.
   - Backups: need deletion plan that addresses offsite/archival backups — deletion must propagate.

8) Audit rights & compliance evidence
   - For enterprise customers: right to audit once/year (or third-party SOC2-type attestations acceptable).
   - If they refuse audits, require additional contractual guarantees and escrow of logs/evidence for incidents.

9) SLA & credits for remediation time
   - Include SLA for uptime and an SLA for incident closure time for security incidents.
   - Credits should be tiered and tied to both availability and time-to-remediate for incidents involving data loss.

Negotiation playbook / concession ladder (quick):
- Must-haves (non-starters to concede): 24h incident notification; certified deletion; export format + 14d delivery; BYOK or equivalent; no training rights without opt-in; deletion propagation to subprocessors.
- Middle ground (we can flex with concessions): deletion timeline to 60d if certified and backup purge schedule; export window to 21d with paid expedited option; limited audit window if we get extended attestations.
- Giveaways (only for significant commercial lift): small liability cap increase for latency/SLA credits; 90-day transition support instead of 30 days; training rights limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry.

Call scripts & one-liners (for legal + solutions calls):
- "We need an explicit export delivery date and signed deletion attestation — vague commitments won't work for our customers with regulatory needs."
- "If training on customer data is important to you, propose a separate paid license with explicit opt-in and data handling commitments."
- "24-hour notification for data-impacting incidents is non-negotiable; we can accept longer timelines for minor operational alerts but not for customer data."

Open questions / items to pull in SRE and product: 
- What formats does Redwood ingest natively today? (parquet vs jsonl vs internal proto) — affects export ask. @Arjun
- How many hours of transition engineering can we reasonably include for standard deals? (default plan vs add-on) — @Claire
- Exact list of caches/kv layers that must be purged for a full deletion cert. Need SRE runbook.

Tasks (actionable):
- Draft specific export clause language (include formats, delivery method, checksum/hash manifest) — owner: me (Maya) — due: 2025-02-24.
- Pull existing Confluence export design + storage/backup diagrams and attach to JIRA LEGAL-4823.
- Confirm with infra whether BYOK is supported across Dedicated and Private offerings; if not, ask for roadmap commit.
- Prepare short negotiation script doc (one-pager) for SEs and AEs to use on calls.

Margin notes / redlines ideas to try in first pass:
- Replace 'reasonable efforts' with explicit timelines and verification steps.
- Add definition for 'customer data' that includes prompts, labels, metadata, and derivative outputs.
- Explicitly require subprocessors to have same deletion obligations and notification windows.
- Add escrow/verification mechanism for deletion (hash manifests + third-party attestation).

Personal reminders: keep the tone firm but pragmatic; the vendor will push back on time windows and deletion certs because of backup complexity. Prioritize customer-facing guarantees over absolute engineering purity — e.g., 'certified deletion within 60 days with manifest' is better than 'immediate deletion but no proof.'

Call notes template (for during negotiation calls):
- Record time/date + attendees.
- Restate what we need in 1-2 sentences.
- Ask vendor for specific timeline and method, then propose our compromise.
- Capture commitments as 'we need this in contract language as [section ref]'.

End of scratchpad.

(Quick search tokens: data-export, certified-deletion, BYOK, subprocessors, incident-notification, model-training-consent)
